_doc: Controlled decode-throughput benchmark. Three operating points per length:
No CROSS-REQUEST prefix sharing: every prompt is a distinct random token
stream. Each request's OWN prefix is warmed before measuring, without which
a bs=max cell never forms -- prefilling 64 x 30k takes minutes while 512
decode tokens take ~15 s, so early requests would finish generating before
KV_SPLITS is pinned on every arm: serve_oscar.sh defaults 48 for vq2 and 8
otherwise, so leaving it unset would compare different decode schedules.
vq2 appears twice because split-K trades off against batch: 48 is worth
-28% at bs=1/100k but +4.5% at batch. Reporting both gives the envelope.
ARTIFACTS ARE SYNTHETIC (random rotations + random codebook) and therefore
THROUGHPUT-VALID / ACCURACY-INVALID. Throughput does not depend on their
contents; this removes the per-model calibration hurdle.
notes: vq2_cuda = vq2_s8 + SGLANG_VQ2_CUDA=1: identical flags and maths, but decode stage-1 runs the CUDA kernel that stages the codebook in shared memory (triton_ops/vq2_cuda_stage1.py) instead of the Triton kernel that gathers it from global. An ADDITIONAL arm; vq2_s8/vq2_s48 are unchanged and still Triton, so the pair is directly comparable at the same split-K. Verified live in the server by torch-profiler kernel counts (2304 calls = 64 steps x 36 layers).
